title: Land Rover LR3 / Discovery 3
verdict: The Discovery that swapped beam axles for air springs and software, and somehow got better off-road for it. It's also heavy, complicated and cheap for a reason, so buy the best-documented one you can find and keep a diagnostic tool in the glovebox.

paragraphs: On 2 April 2004 Land Rover replaced the last Discovery that still rode on 1970 Range Rover bones with something completely new. The Discovery 3, sold in North America as the LR3, kept the family's stepped roof and upright glass but threw away the beam axles, coil springs and ladder-frame simplicity of the [[land-rover/discovery-1|Discovery Series I]] and its successor. In their place came height-adjustable air suspension at all four corners, a body welded to its own chassis, and a rotary knob that told the truck what kind of ground it was on. Purists sneered. Then the reviews arrived.

story.heading: A CLEAN SHEET FROM THE FORD YEARS
paragraphs: The Discovery 3 was the first Land Rover designed after the company and BMW parted ways in 2000, and it arrived almost four years after Ford bought the brand. It was revealed in April 2004 and made its international debut at the British International Motor Show that May. In North America and the Middle East it was badged LR3, partly because of negative quality associations with the Discovery name and, Land Rover said, an American preference for alphanumeric model names; the second Freelander became the LR2 there too.

Everything under the skin came from the Ford family. American trucks got a 300 hp 4.4-litre Jaguar-derived V8 or, in early years, a 216 hp 4.0-litre Ford V6. In Europe the big seller was meant to be the 2.7-litre TDV6, a Ford/PSA-developed V6 diesel with 195 hp and 440 Nm. The diesel came with a six-speed manual as standard; a ZF six-speed automatic was optional on the diesel and standard on the V8, and every version had a two-speed transfer box and permanent four-wheel drive.

story.heading: INTEGRATED BODY FRAME AND CROSS-LINKED AIR
paragraphs: Land Rover called the new structure Integrated Body Frame. The engine bay and passenger cell are built as a monocoque, then joined to a basic ladder frame that carries the gearbox and suspension. Land Rover claimed the best of both worlds; critics pointed at a curb weight of 5,426 lb. It is heavier than a pure monocoque but adds strength and toughness, and Land Rover tucked the vital parts up into the body-frame to protect ground clearance.

The suspension is independent double wishbones on air springs, like the [[range-rover/l322|Range Rover L322]]. It can lower for loading, run low at speed and rise for clearance, from 7.3 in at standard height to 9.4 in at off-road height. Off-road, the air springs are cross-linked so that when one wheel drops the other rises, mimicking a beam axle. If the chassis touches the ground at off-road height, the system senses the lost load and lifts another inch. Britain and Europe also got a five-seat, coil-sprung base TDV6 without Terrain Response.

story.heading: A KNOB THAT DOES THE THINKING
paragraphs: Terrain Response was the headline. Instead of asking the driver to choose gears, ride height, locking strategy and throttle response, the Discovery 3 offered a dial with settings that included Grass-Gravel-Snow, Sand, Mud and Ruts, and Rock Crawl. Land Rover said engineers studied more than 50 off-road surfaces to calibrate it. In Rock Crawl the suspension goes to full height with maximum articulation, the differentials lock and the driver is prompted to select low range; in Sand the traction control is primed for wheelspin and the throttle is sharpened.

Underneath, a computer-controlled, progressively locking centre differential kept torque flowing, and a similar locking differential was available for the rear axle. The press loved it. Richard Hammond called it the 'best 4x4 of all time', Australia's 4WD press named it 4WD of the Year, and Jeremy Clarkson drove one to the summit of Cnoc an Fhreiceadain near Tongue in northern Scotland, a 307 m hill no vehicle had reached before.

story.heading: LIVING WITH ONE NOW
paragraphs: The bargain is obvious: Bring a Trailer LR3s have recently sold for between about $3,000 and $23,000, with a median near $9,000, for a seven-seat truck that will follow a [[land-cruiser/100-series|100 Series]] almost anywhere. The catch is everything that makes it clever. Air springs, compressors and height sensors age, the electronic parking brake jams, heavy weight eats front lower-arm bushes, and PistonHeads notes that in 2012 Warranty Direct logged more claims on the Discovery 3 than on any other used car from a European maker.

Diesel buyers outside the US also have to accept the TDV6's crankshaft and bearing failures, which Land Rover's own bulletin blames mainly on bearing shells located incorrectly at assembly. American trucks dodge that bullet with the V8, which drinks fuel at an EPA-rated 12–13 mpg in town but is the engine the US aftermarket knows best. Either way, an IIDTool or similar Land Rover diagnostic tool turns most of the scary warnings into Saturday jobs.

story.heading: LEGACY
paragraphs: The Discovery 3 platform underpinned the Range Rover Sport, and in 2009 it became the Discovery 4 (LR4 in North America), which kept the Integrated Body Frame and added restyled lights, a new grille and smoother bumpers. Late Discovery 3s from 2008–09 had already gained body-colour bumpers, clear side indicators and a Harman/Kardon stereo upgrade. Today the LR3 is the cheapest way into air-sprung, Terrain Response Land Rover off-roading, with a busy aftermarket of lift rods, sliders and coil conversions behind it.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · G4, TOP GEAR AND A ROBOT
callout.title: The family seven-seater that drove itself to fourth place
paragraphs: Land Rover ran the Discovery 3 in its 2006 G4 Challenge alongside the Range Rover Sport, in standard mechanical form apart from added Land Rover off-road equipment. On television, Top Gear sent Jeremy Clarkson up Cnoc an Fhreiceadain in one, and Richard Hammond declared it the best 4x4 of all time.

The oddest entry on its CV is the DARPA Urban Challenge, where a driverless LR3 finished fourth. A plan to assemble Discovery 3s from knock-down kits at Ford's Vsevolozhsk plant in Russia never happened; it was cancelled in 2007.

engineering_intro: The Discovery 3 is built around Land Rover's Integrated Body Frame: a monocoque engine bay and cabin joined to a ladder frame that carries the gearbox and suspension. All four wheels hang on independent double wishbones with air springs, cross-linked off-road to behave like a beam axle. Drive goes through a two-speed transfer box (2.93:1 low) with a progressively locking centre differential, and an electronically locking rear differential was available. Terrain Response, Hill Descent Control, four-wheel electronic traction control and an electronic parking brake round out a truck that is as much a network of control modules as a 4x4.

buying_checks.head: TDV6 bottom end
buying_checks.body: Land Rover bulletin SSM71816 covers crankshaft and main-bearing failures on the TDV6, caused mainly by bearing shells located incorrectly at assembly and by shells rotating in use. Listen for a rumble or knock that worsens under load, and an oil-pressure light at low revs. Failures are rare but very expensive, and the UK has a whole industry selling reconditioned TDV6 engines.

buying_checks.head: Air suspension
buying_checks.body: Run it through every height with the engine on, check it sits level, and leave it overnight to see whether a corner sags. Leaks, height-sensor faults and tired compressors are the usual causes. A compressor that runs for a long time, overheats or slows before cutting out is on its way out.

buying_checks.head: Electronic parking brake
buying_checks.body: Check that it applies and releases cleanly, more than once. PistonHeads says the EPB often clogs with dirt and a replacement unit can cost over £1,000; owners of the closely related LR4 on LandRoverWorld describe $900–2,200 shop quotes for actuator and cable work.

buying_checks.head: Front lower arms and bushes
buying_checks.body: A 5,400 lb truck wears out its bushes, ball joints, wheel bearings and brakes. Look for split boots and oil weeping from the hydraulic rear bushes of the front lower arms, and budget for seized bolts if they need doing.

buying_checks.head: ZF six-speed automatic
buying_checks.body: Feel for judder and harsh shifts and ask when the fluid was last changed. Land Rover's long fluid interval was optimistic; PistonHeads suggests changing it about five times as often. Coolant can also reach the gearbox through the heat exchanger in the radiator, so look for milky fluid.

buying_checks.head: TDV6 belts, flywheel and EGR
buying_checks.body: Ask for proof of the timing belt, tensioner, pulleys and water pump; PistonHeads advises doing them within six years or 60,000 miles. Manual trucks can eat dual-mass flywheels and clutches at low mileage, and EGR valves often fail.

buying_checks.head: 4.4 V8 cooling
buying_checks.body: The plastic thermostat housing and its coolant tube can crack and drip. Check around the front of the engine for dried coolant, and make sure the temperature gauge stays steady on a long run.

buying_checks.head: Electrics, A/C and recalls
buying_checks.body: Expect warning lights and test everything: central locking, windows, rear wiper, sat-nav, A/C (compressors and pipes corrode), battery and alternator. In the US, run the VIN for open recalls, including the 2005–06 steering-wheel clockspring campaign.

repairs.title: Rebuild or replace the air suspension compressor
repairs.cost: Rebuild kit vs. complete compressor kit
repairs.symptoms: Slow height changes, suspension faults, a compressor that gets very hot and slows before cutting out with an error. One DISCO3.CO.UK owner's unit reached 90°C in about 90 seconds.
repairs.fix: Owners rebuild the original Hitachi with a piston glide ring, fresh desiccant and filters and an aluminium dryer cap, or fit a complete new unit. Don't wait: a failing compressor lets the dryer's silica turn to dust, which can reach and damage the valve blocks. Expect seized unions at the dryer (penetrating oil and time), use silicone grease on the O-rings, check the bracket bushes, and fit a new relay. Converting to the later AMK compressor is a factory-approved upgrade but needs a software update.
repairs.tools: Sockets, penetrating oil, silicone grease, push-fit couplings if pipes must be cut · compressor overhaul kit JPO500010 · dryer VUB504700 · relay YWB500220

repairs.title: Front air spring or strut
repairs.symptoms: One corner leans or drops, the fault keeps coming back, or you hear air hiss over bumps. A soapy-water test shows the leak.
repairs.fix: Pull the suspension fuse, support the body on stands and remove the wheel. Support the lower strut bolt with a jack, remove the two top nuts in the wheel well and the third in the engine bay (lift the heat shield first), and crack the air line slowly, letting any pressure bleed off before it comes apart. Either fit a complete strut or swap the bag onto the old damper with new O-rings and spacers, then refit and let the system fill. Some owners recalibrate the height afterwards.
repairs.tools: 15 mm sockets, swivel, breaker bar, 12/13 mm spanner for the air line, jack and stands · front strut RNB501580 or air spring LR016403 · seal LR016412

repairs.title: Ride height sensor replacement
repairs.symptoms: Uneven ride height, suspension warning lights, or a truck that won't hold the height it's asked for. Height-sensor faults are one of the electrical causes of air-suspension trouble.
repairs.fix: Each corner has its own sensor linked to a suspension arm. Unplug it, unbolt the sensor and its link, fit the new one and check the arm moves freely. Repair a corroded plug with the harness repair kit rather than living with it. The suspension usually needs calibrating after a sensor is replaced; Gap's IIDTool offers an individual sensor calibration that doesn't need a level floor.

repairs.title: Electronic parking brake actuator
repairs.time: Many hours the first time (one LR4 owner took 11)
repairs.cost: LR4 owners report $900–2,200 shop quotes; a gear kit is cheap
repairs.symptoms: The parking brake won't apply or release, or the motor grinds or whines without effect. A seized EPB can leave the truck stuck.
repairs.fix: In an emergency, PistonHeads notes the EPB can be released manually with the jack handle through a metal loop behind a plastic panel. For the repair, the actuator sits ahead of the rear frame rail with very little clearance; owners remove the module and cables, then fit a gear repair kit or a complete actuator. One LandRoverWorld LR4 owner traced his fault to the cable adjusting bolt being threaded in too far and reset it to five turns into the tube. Check the rear shoes and their hardware while you're there.

repairs.title: Front lower control arms and bushes
repairs.time: 45 min per side on a lift; a full day if bolts are seized
repairs.cost: One owner was quoted $1,400 for both arms plus alignment
repairs.symptoms: Clunks, vague steering, tyre wear, split boots and oil leaking from the hydraulic rear bush.
repairs.fix: Soak the fixings for days beforehand. Many bolts come out with heat or a drift; seized ones are cut with a reciprocating saw and carbide blades, which is why Lucky8 sells arm kits with new hardware. You may need a puller to push the drive shaft back through the hub. Fit the new arms or bushes and get an alignment straight away; one owner warns a badly misaligned truck can drop to its bump stops on the way to the shop, and a restart pumps it back up.
repairs.tools: Torque wrench to about 300 Nm, 18/21/22 mm sockets, reciprocating saw with carbide blades, heat, 3-jaw puller · arm kit with hardware · bush LR073366

repairs.title: ZF 6HP26 fluid, pan and filter
repairs.cost: About the price of a service kit
repairs.symptoms: Judder, flare or harsh shifts, an unknown service history, or a weeping valve body sleeve.
repairs.fix: The filter is built into the plastic pan, so you replace the pan. Drain, drop the pan, and replace the valve body sleeve (a common leak point) while it's open. Refill with ZF-spec fluid and follow the factory fill-and-level procedure with the fluid at the specified temperature. Workshop data quotes 9.5 litres for a dry fill; a pan change takes far less, so some owners repeat it to refresh more of the fluid.
repairs.tools: Sockets, fluid pump, scan tool or thermometer for the level check · pan LR007474 · sleeve TZV500010 · ATF TYK500050

repairs.title: TDV6 timing belt and water pump
repairs.symptoms: Due on age or mileage, no paperwork, or a weeping water pump. PistonHeads also notes the oil-pump casing that the timing-belt tensioner bolts to can snap off.
repairs.fix: PistonHeads advises replacing the belt, tensioner, small pulleys and water pump within six years or 60,000 miles. Lock the engine with the correct timing tools before removing the old belt, fit the full kit and pump, and turn the engine by hand before starting. Note there are separate Euro 3 and Euro 4 belt kits for the 2.7, so match the kit to your engine.

repairs.title: 4.4 V8 thermostat housing and coolant tube
repairs.time: ≈ 2–3 hours plus an hour to bleed
repairs.symptoms: A slow coolant drip from a crack in the plastic thermostat housing, low coolant, rising temperature.
repairs.fix: Drain the coolant, remove the engine cover, air box and intake, the throttle body and the hoses to the housing, then the eight T30 Torx bolts; the assembly is sealed by three O-rings, not sealant. Fit the new LR005631 assembly as one piece (one owner split it, damaged an O-ring and made a new leak) and tighten the bolts evenly. Refill with OAT coolant and bleed patiently through the expansion tank and bleed screw, ideally with a vacuum filler.
repairs.tools: 6/8/10/13 mm sockets, T30 Torx, wobble extensions, pick, vacuum coolant filler · LR005631 · LRN2279 coolant

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: On 18-inch wheels, 265/65R18 or 285/60R18 (about 31 in) fit at factory height without modification. 275/65R18 (about 32 in) is about the biggest that works at stock height, and owners report it needs the front-left height-sensor wire zip-tied to the frame rail and a little liner reshaping; one owner's 285/65R18s rubbed slightly at full lock. With lift rods, 275/65R18 is the common choice. One owner advises staying under 32 in overall.

Sort of. Land Rover's Integrated Body Frame builds the engine bay and cabin as a monocoque, then joins them to a basic ladder frame that carries the gearbox and suspension. It is heavier than a pure monocoque but stronger and tougher.

In the US the choice is the 300 hp 4.4 V8 (all years) or the 216 hp 4.0 V6 (2005–07). The V8 is the common one, shared with the 2006–09 Range Rover Sport and L322 Range Rover. Elsewhere most trucks have the 195 hp, 440 Nm 2.7 TDV6, which is far more economical but carries crank-bearing and timing-belt risks.

faq.q: Which years are the best to buy?
faq.a: Later is better, within reason. The 2005 LR3 has the most NHTSA complaints (96, against 8 for 2008 and 3 for 2009) and five recalls, and ReRev names 2005 the one to avoid and 2008–09 the most reliable. Raw complaint counts aren't adjusted for how many were sold, though, and PistonHeads still calls any phase-one Discovery 3 a high-risk purchase, so a thick service file beats a late build date.

faq.q: Is the TDV6 crank failure real?
faq.a: Yes, though it's uncommon. Land Rover bulletin SSM71816 covers crankshaft and main-bearing failures, mainly caused by incorrectly located bearing shells at assembly. Symptoms are a knock or rumble that worsens under load, sometimes with the oil-pressure light. Carbuyer calls it rare, unpredictable and very costly.
7,716 lb (3,500 kg) braked and 1,654 lb (750 kg) unbraked, according to Land Rover's launch specifications.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: EPA ratings for the V8 are 12–13 mpg city and 17 highway, depending on year; the V6 is rated 13/18 for 2005. In the UK, PistonHeads quotes 27.2 mpg (imperial) for the automatic TDV6 and 18.8 mpg for the V8.

The cheap route is lift rods, which replace the links on the factory height sensors so the air suspension sits about 2–2.5 in higher (Proud Rhino, Terrafirma and Lucky8 make them). A diagnostic tool such as Gap's IIDTool can change the programmed heights instead. If you've had enough of air, Terrafirma sells +2 in coil conversions and Old Man Emu coil springs for the LR3 are sold too.

Every truck has a computer-controlled, progressively locking centre differential. A locking rear differential (Land Rover's electronic torque managed unit) was optional. Terrain Response controls how hard both lock in each mode.

faq.q: What goes wrong with the air suspension?
faq.a: Leaking air springs, height sensors, compressors and the electrics. A failing compressor overheats and slows; if ignored, the dryer desiccant can break down and damage the valve blocks. Many owners rebuild the Hitachi compressor; the later AMK unit needs a software update to fit.

faq.q: My parking brake is stuck. How do I release it?
faq.a: PistonHeads says a seized EPB can be released manually using the jack handle through a metal loop behind a plastic panel. The underlying fault is usually the actuator or its cable adjustment, and dirt build-up is a known cause.

faq.q: What's the difference between an LR3 and a Discovery 3?
faq.a: Nothing structural: LR3 is the North American and Middle Eastern name. The engines differ by market, with the V8 and V6 petrols in North America and the TDV6 diesel as the main engine elsewhere.
Land Rover's launch specification quotes a 700 mm (27.6 in) wading depth. Raise the suspension to off-road height before you go in.

baseline_service.intro: Most LR3s have had cheap ownership for years, and on this truck deferred maintenance shows up as warning lights. Baseline the fluids in the ZF gearbox, transfer box and diffs that many owners never touch, do the TDV6 timing belt unless there's proof, and check the air suspension and parking brake with a diagnostic tool while the truck is on stands.
